copy.hubDawn: a line is a sentence about what you value, made from something that really happened. no one hands it to you.
copy.hubDawnReturn: welcome back. a line can be tuned any time, or you can make a new one.
copy.none: nothing here yet, and that's fine. when you'd like to, make the first one.
copy.beforeIntro: thanks for coming by. a quick look at how it feels right now, only if you'd like.
copy.afterNote: any shift counts, and so does none.
copy.valueDawn: pick a word that already matters. it can be small.
copy.valueTeach: people who write about what they value tend to feel steadier afterward. it works best when the value is their own.
copy.ownVerbDawn: good word. we'll build the line around it.
copy.momentDawn: something small and recent. a minute, not a memory.
copy.momentTeach: using a name, the way a friend would, puts a little distance between a person and a line. that can make it easier to believe.
copy.momentTeachFirst: a line grounded in something that really happened is easier to believe than a big claim.
copy.momentLabel: a small moment, finishing the sentence
copy.shapeDawn: pick the one that feels closest. you can change any word next.
copy.tuneDawn: change any word. select one and tap a word to swap it in, or write it all your own way.
copy.tuneLead: sometimes, quietly, usually: tap to add
copy.tryDawn: read it slowly. notice how it lands. any answer is welcome.
copy.truthLow: thanks for being honest. a smaller line may fit better. a believable line does more than a big one.
copy.truthMid: that's a good sign. it's close, and a word or two can bring it closer.
copy.truthHigh: that sounds like it fits. thanks for taking it seriously.
copy.keptDawn: {name} made that, from something real. it's in the book now.
copy.keptDawnNoName: made from something real. it's in the book now.
copy.doneThanks: thanks for coming by. the line is there whenever you want it.
copy.todayEmpty: when you'd like, make a line of your own. it takes a few minutes.
copy.bookNote: lines made from values and real moments. tap one to see if it's still true.
copy.whyIntro: three ideas sit under this practice. each has a source and an honest label.

moments: yesterday, when a friend needed a hand
this morning, when staying in was easier
yesterday, when a small answer was easier
last week, in a quick text
the other day, when someone asked what fits
the other day, in the grocery store
last week, picking up the phone
the other day, starting before feeling ready
this week, reading about something new
last night, asking a friend for more
this morning, with a slow computer
last week, with a friend running late
this week, a ride for a friend
last weekend, an hour of help
this morning, over a warm drink
yesterday, a better way to do something
yesterday, a small promise to a friend
this week, being there when it was said
last month, a call that was promised
this week, picking what to do
this week, in a long meeting
last night, with a slow breath
this week, with a new face
today, a few minutes just for fun

why.text: writing briefly about what matters, in one's own words, has helped people stay steady when things felt threatening. it works best when the value is their own.

source.label: Steele, 1988; Cohen & Sherman, 2014, Annual Review of Psychology
source.evidence: solid for short-term effects in many studies. effects vary by person and setting.

why.text: talking to yourself by name, the way a friend would, adds a little distance. that can make a hard moment feel lighter.

source.label: Kross et al., 2014, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
source.evidence: good lab evidence for the distance effect. real-life effects are smaller and still being studied.

why.text: big positive statements can backfire for people with low self-esteem: the further a line sits from what they believe, the worse it can feel. so lines here start small, from real moments.

source.label: Wood, Perunovic & Lee, 2009, Psychological Science
source.evidence: one well-known set of studies. it's why every line here is checked against how true it feels.
